hook: The teacher of the deaf who invented the telephone.

pages.x: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Edinburgh in 1847. His mother was going deaf, and his father and grandfather taught people how to speak well. His father invented a set of symbols for every sound the human mouth can make.

As a boy he taught the family dog to growl steadily while he moved its mouth with his hands, until it seemed to say "How are you, grandma?" With his brother he also built a talking head that cried "Mama!"
After his two brothers died of tuberculosis, the family moved to Canada in 1870. He went on to Boston to teach deaf children to speak. One of his pupils, Mabel Hubbard, became his wife.

Trying to send several telegraph messages along one wire, he found a way to turn the sound of a voice into a changing electric current, and back again. He filed his patent in 1876, hours before a rival.
pages.fx: The telephone let people talk across cities and oceans, and changed business and daily life around the world.

pages.x: On 10 March 1876 he spoke the first words by telephone, to his assistant in the next room: "Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you." Watson later said Bell had just spilled acid on his clothes.

pages.t: Talking on a beam of light
pages.x: In 1880 he sent his voice along a beam of sunlight with his photophone, which he called his greatest invention, greater than the telephone.
pages.fx: It was the ancestor of fibre optics, the threads of glass that carry the internet today.

pages.x: In 1887 the parents of a deaf and blind six-year-old, Helen Keller, came to him for help. He sent them to a school for the blind, which sent a young teacher, Anne Sullivan. Keller later dedicated her life story to him.
At his summer home in Nova Scotia he built giant kites and flying machines. In 1919 his team's hydrofoil boat set a world speed record on water, 114 km an hour.
He thought the telephone a nuisance, and would not have one in his study. When he died in 1922, every telephone in North America was silent for one minute in his honour.
Bell invented the telephone, and spent his life helping deaf people to communicate.
pts: A lifelong teacher of the deaf
Sent the first voice message on a beam of light
